title: Expense Management Best Practices Guide: How to Choose the Right Finance & Accounting Platform
description: Practical expense management best practices guidance with workflow design, controls, measurement, and a readiness checklist.
author: Emily Nakamura

sections.title: Define the expense policy before automation
sections.body: Document eligible expenses, spending limits, approval thresholds, required receipts, per-diem rules, and exceptions by role or location. Make the policy easy to find and explain who can approve an exception. Software can enforce rules consistently, but unclear or outdated policies will produce disputes faster when they are automated.

sections.title: Design the submission experience
sections.body: Test mobile receipt capture, required fields, currencies, mileage, project or client codes, and handling of missing receipts. Check how the system reads receipt data and how employees correct mistakes. Make the submission path usable for people who travel or have limited connectivity. Avoid requiring unnecessary personal data or making employees upload sensitive information to an unapproved channel.

sections.title: Set approval and segregation controls
sections.body: Map who submits, reviews, approves, reimburses, and reconciles each expense type. Test thresholds, manager changes, delegate approvals, duplicate claims, and self-approval prevention. Keep an audit trail for edits and exceptions. Ensure that the person approving an expense has enough context to judge policy compliance without gaining broad access to unrelated employee records.

sections.title: Connect finance and payment systems
sections.body: Test integration with accounting, payroll, corporate cards, travel booking, and payment providers. Define which system owns the employee, account code, currency, and reimbursement status. Test duplicate transactions, refunds, chargebacks, failed syncs, and month-end cutoffs. Reconcile totals against a trusted statement before relying on automated exports.

sections.title: Detect fraud and protect privacy
sections.body: Review duplicate receipt detection, unusual amounts, merchant rules, audit logs, and escalation paths. Treat alerts as a prompt for review rather than proof of misconduct. Limit access to receipts and employee details, set retention rules, and verify export and deletion behavior. Consult qualified finance, HR, and privacy owners for local requirements.

sections.title: Measure cycle time and accuracy
sections.body: Track time from submission to reimbursement, rejection reasons, missing documentation, duplicate rate, exception volume, and reconciliation differences. Compare results with a baseline and inspect a sample of claims for false flags. Faster processing is not an improvement if it creates incorrect reimbursements or pushes the review burden to finance.

sections.title: Model the total cost
sections.body: Include per-user licenses, transaction volume, card programs, OCR or AI usage, accounting integrations, implementation, training, and administration. Verify current pricing and limits directly with the vendor. Estimate how cost changes as employee count and travel volume grow. Include the effort to maintain policies and update accounting mappings.

sections.title: Go-live checklist
sections.body: Pilot a full expense cycle from submission through approval, reimbursement, and reconciliation. Verify access controls, duplicate handling, exports, and exception paths. Keep a manual fallback for outages and define who owns policy changes. Review the workflow after changes to accounting rules, travel policy, or payment providers.
